method.tool: scratchpad/tools/coverage_search.py --whole-words --regex, eight term sets (search/C8/S1..S8-*.json, terms in terms.txt)
method.record_check: search/C8/recgrep.py: independent front-matter grep of records/*/*/*.md
method.verification: search/C8/verify.py plus a manual re-check of four records for editorial artifacts
method.layers: RENDERED (R*, honest_limit or guard only) / LOADED / IDENTIFIED / OTHER / NOTHING; N used in tables for NOTHING

sub_questions.label: Women's lives in their own words; any writing by women; nuns
Women leading, preaching, deacons, priests; 'wives, submit'; were women lesser
The enslaved: owned, freed, thought wrong, 'slaves obey', one table, the tortured witnesses
Marriage: age, consent, mixed marriage, widows remarrying, divorce, adultery
Sex in marriage, virginity ranked above marriage, contraception, abortion and exposure, extreme asceticism
Gay people and same-sex relations (never faced as asked)
A wife beaten and the church's word (Facilitator ground)

detail.F5-I: f5-i-03 women in their own words: alx, gallic, hal, witt; f5-i-01 ordinary day: ijc. No demo for f5-i-04 children or f5-i-05 the enslaved in any world.
detail.F5-T: none: f5-t-01 (what marriage meant) has no demonstration in any world.
detail.F6-P: f6-p-06 women's authority: alx, cappadocian, desert, don, hal, ijc, pahc, syr (8); missing gallic, lpc, rzg, witt. Also f6-p-01 someone-like-me x10, f6-p-02 x5, f6-p-03 x1 (gallic), f6-p-05 x2 (don, ijc).
detail.F6-T: f6-t-03 divorce: alx, desert, hal, pahc, syr (5); missing cappadocian, don, gallic, ijc, lpc, rzg, witt. f6-t-01 hell: alx, hal.
detail.F6-E: f6-e-01 (clearest outside account; the question for the two enslaved women, C8-07): no demonstration anywhere. f6-e-02 martyr wish: don, witt. The Pliny question is answered only by records: pahc (quote, story, term, limit) and the guards hal.limit.martyrdom, ijc.limit.earlier-windows.

findings.title: The library holds what the records say they cannot give
findings.detail: Vendored and unrecorded: Clement Strom. IV.8 and II.23 in English (anf02 L38538, L38643, L34787) against alx.limit.marriage and the silence on women; Basil's canons on abortion, same-sex acts, a hatchet raised at a wife and marriage without a master's consent (npnf208 L34979, L35084, L35123, L36510); Nazianzen Or. 37 (npnf207 L35864); Life of Macrina L120, L138, L158; Calvin Inst. and Second Helvetic ch. XXIX against rzg.limit.no-teaching-on-wealth-or-marriage; Thecla and CTh 3.7, 4.7, 5.10 in worlds that render none of it.

findings.title: Two records contradict a vendored text or rest on a missing one
findings.detail: syr.limit.marriage and syr.demo.marriage-ending say no text speaks to Christian marriage or its ending, but the Book of the Laws of Countries (anf08 L68966-68985, mapped to syr) states what Edessa Christians do about an unchaste wife or sister. cappadocian.story.slave-market-sermon rests on Nyssa's Ecclesiastes homily, which is unvendored; the line is a paraphrase. hal.dw.marriage-ending is gentler than Jerome's own answer in Ep. 55 (npnf206 L12992-13029).

findings.title: Demos are thin exactly where the questions are hardest
findings.detail: F5-T has no demo anywhere; F6-E-01 (the tortured enslaved women) has none; F6-T-03 divorce has five of twelve worlds; no demo for children (F5-I-04) or the enslaved (F5-I-05). S6 has no record in any world; S3 is carried by records in three worlds (cappadocian, gallic, pahc), by guards in four, and by no record in five.

findings.title: Perpetua and Egeria are the library's women's own words and both sit outside every record
findings.detail: anf03 L59560 (Perpetua "described by her own hand"; also Felicitas, an enslaved woman) is mapped to lpc and deliberately excluded as pre-246. Egeria (L3339-3403 Edessa, L3790 Marthana) is mapped to desert and syr, which say no woman's line survives.

not_checked: Record bodies below the front matter were read only for the cited records; the grep covers front matter fields only.
Vendored hits are tool counts plus the contexts quoted; hits marked "not read" or "context not read" are unconfirmed leads, not claims.
Many S5 and S7 tool hits are noise ("school", "infant", "lust"); only passages whose context was read are cited.
Latin, Greek, French, German and Dutch vendored files were counted, not read (Augustine Latin, Calvin Opera, Ordonnances, Synodicon).
canon/sealed_probes/ was not read. No model call, no network. lpc and some pahc and don records are status draft; which are in the compiled package was not checked.
